text: For the choirmaster. On the gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah.<note>Gittith: probably a musical term, perhaps a tune or an instrument; the meaning is uncertain.</note>

versions.text: For the choirmaster. On the gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
versions.explanation: The transliterated term "gittith" is opaque to hearers and readers; a brief footnote clarifies that it is an uncertain musical designation.

text: How lovely are your dwelling places, LORD of hosts!

versions.text: How lovely is your dwelling place, LORD of hosts!
versions.explanation: The Hebrew noun מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶיךָ is plural, and the predicate יְדִידוֹת agrees with it in the plural. The plural also reads well aloud and preserves the poetic fullness of the temple imagery.

text: My soul longs, yes, faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for joy to the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young — at your altars, LORD of hosts, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who dwell in your house; they are always praising you. Selah

Blessed are those whose strength is in you, in whose hearts are the pilgrim highways.<note>Hebrew reads simply "highways in their hearts"; the image is of roads leading up to the sanctuary, hence the sense of a pilgrim's journey.</note>

versions.text: Blessed are those whose strength is in you, in whose hearts are the highways to Zion.
versions.explanation: "to Zion" is not in the Hebrew, which reads simply "highways in their hearts." If the interpretive expansion is kept, it should be marked; "pilgrim highways" conveys the sense without adding a place name absent from the text.

versions.text: Blessed are those whose strength is in you, in whose hearts are the pilgrim highways.
versions.explanation: The wording is a fair rendering, but the qualifier "pilgrim" is interpretive and not present in the Hebrew. A short footnote lets the hearer know what the bare Hebrew says and why the image is understood as a journey to the sanctuary, without altering the smooth oral reading.

text: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the early rain covers it with blessings.
They go from strength to strength, till each appears before God in Zion.
LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah
Look upon our shield, O God; look with favor on the face of your anointed.
Better is one day in your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
For the LORD God is a sun and shield; the LORD bestows favor and honor. No good thing does he withhold from those who walk uprightly.
LORD of hosts, blessed is the one who trusts in you.
